slide/row: Here is a row of five numbers, x, and a filter of three weights, w: minus one, zero and one.
slide/first: Lay the filter over the first three entries. Multiply each pair and add: minus one, plus zero, plus four. That is three, the first output.
slide/step: Now slide the filter one step to the right and do the same: minus two, plus zero, plus four. Two.
slide/last: One more step gives minus four plus one, minus three. Then the filter runs out of room: five inputs, three outputs.
slide/dot: Each output is a dot product between the filter and the window under it, and the same three weights are used at every position.
edges/diff: This filter takes the last entry of each window minus the first: how much the input changes across it.
edges/step: Slide it along a row of pixel brightnesses that jumps from one up to six. Where the row climbs, the output is five.
edges/flat: Where the row is flat, the minus one and the plus one cancel, giving zero. Where it falls, the output goes negative.
edges/detect: So this filter is an edge detector. Any filter answers most strongly where the input looks like the filter itself.
edges/sum: A filter of all ones, one, one, one, looks like an even patch, and it just adds up each window: three, eight, thirteen, eighteen and fourteen. It peaks where the row is brightest, not at the edge.
grid/image: An image is a grid, so its filter is a grid too: here three by three, with ones on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere.
grid/patch: Lay it on the top left three by three patch, multiply all nine pairs, and add. Only the diagonal counts: one, plus one, plus zero. Two.
grid/step: Now slide it one step to the right. Output row zero, column one uses the patch one column over: rows zero to two, columns one to three. Its diagonal is two, plus three, plus two: seven.
grid/rule: In general, call the output's row number i and its column number j. Output i, j comes from the patch that starts i rows down and j columns across: rows i to i plus two, columns j to j plus two.
grid/rest: One row down, the last two patches give two and four. So a four by four image gives a two by two output: two, seven, two and four.
grid/map: The output is a map of how well each patch matches the filter. Seven marks the brightest diagonal line in the image.
